Pager Tower (Only Applies to Ultra Realistic)
Lets players block a pager number so its pages never reach them. Useful against griefers in PvP.
Lets a player send one page to every pager on the network with the Broadcast button. Turn this off on busy servers to cut down on spam.
Enables the emergency SOS button, which pages everyone on the network at once and attaches the sender's location (unless location sharing is Off).
How long a fresh battery powers a pager before it dies and must be replaced. Measured in in-game time. Replace batteries from the pager's right-click menu using a Battery item.
How loud the pager's notification beep plays. Applies to every beep the pager makes.

Controls who can reach who.
Anyone: any pager can page any other (the default).
Same faction only: members of different factions cannot page each other, so rival groups can't eavesdrop or spam. Players who are not in a faction can always be reached.

Adds a town-wide GLOBAL tab to every pager: a shared channel anyone with a pager can read and post to, reaching everyone regardless of saved contacts or faction. It still obeys the signal mode, receive-only mode, send cooldown and per-person blocking.
Cannot use a pager at all

What the Illiterate trait does to pagers.
No effect: illiterate characters use pagers normally.
Cannot read pages: page text and sender names appear as ??? for an illiterate character, and the pages they send can only contain digits, spaces and dashes - a numeric-code device. Their pager still beeps and shows numbers.
Cannot use a pager: an illiterate character cannot open a pager or a tower console at all. The pager still beeps in their pocket, and they can still set up or pack away a tower.
Share your location on a page

Whether a page can include where the sender is standing. The recipient then sees the coordinates plus distance and a compass bearing.
Off: location is never shared.
Ask each time: the sender ticks a box per page (the default).
Always on: every page carries the sender's location.
An SOS still shares location unless this is set to Off.
Log pages to a server file
Appends every routed page (sender, recipient, text, delivered/queued/blocked) to PagerMod_PageLog.txt in the server's Zomboid folder. For admins/moderation.
How many pages a single pager keeps. Once it is full, the oldest page is dropped to make room for a new one.
The longest message a player can put in one page, counted in characters.
Play a beep and show an on-screen alert (with a preview of the message) whenever a new page comes in.
Pages may contain digits, spaces and dashes only - all letters are stripped out. Turns pagers into a numeric-code device.

What pagers can do.
Send and receive: normal two-way paging (the default).
Receive only: pagers can only receive pages - the compose, reply and group features are hidden.

Quick bundles of the options below.
Custom: nothing is overridden - every option on this page applies as you set it (the default).
Convenient: the relaxed defaults - map-wide signal, full two-way paging and every feature on.
Almost Realistic: a barely-functional pocket pager - 1 saved page, 16 characters, no location, no read receipts, no SOS, no blocking, no broadcast (still map-wide).
Ultra Realistic: everything in Almost Realistic, plus pagers can only receive (not send), and the network is map-wide only until the power dies, then needs a built, powered pager tower.
A preset overrides the matching options below.
Notifies the sender once the person they paged has opened and read the message.
Minimum number of seconds a player must wait between sending pages. Helps stop spam and griefing on PvP servers. Set to 0 for no limit (the default).

How far pages travel.
Map-wide: pagers reach anywhere on the map (the default - pagers are your long-range tier, with walkie-talkies for medium range and voice chat up close).
Limited range: a page only arrives if the recipient is within the distance set below.
Powered tower only (after power dies): pages reach map-wide while the electricity grid is still on, but once the power goes out the network only works through a built, powered pager tower's coverage - so the pager network dies with the grid unless someone keeps a tower running on a generator.
Powered tower only: the network ALWAYS needs a built, powered pager tower in range, even while the grid is up.

The reach distance in tiles (1 tile is about 1 metre), used by two signal modes: in Limited range it's the furthest a page can travel between sender and recipient; in Powered tower mode it's each tower's coverage radius (both ends of a page must be within it).

How much pager loot the world has, as a multiplier on the weights pagers already carry in electronics, police, comms and vehicle containers - so they still turn up where they make sense, there are just more or fewer of them.
Vanilla (unchanged) is the default and touches no loot table at all. In Build 41, where the pager is not a vanilla item, the higher settings are also what puts it into electronics loot in the first place.
Only affects containers the world has not generated yet.

What the tower base station (000-0001) itself can do.
Send and receive: the tower can send pages and be paged - its console has an inbox.
Send only: the tower can only send pages; it cannot be paged.
The most pager towers a single player may have set up at once. Each tower is its own node with its own number and coverage circle. Set to 0 for no limit. Admins are exempt.

What a deployed pager tower needs to run (Powered tower mode).
Grid or generator: mains electricity OR a running generator nearby (the default).
Generator only: only a running, fuelled generator beside it (ignores the power grid).
None: towers always work, no power needed.

A pocket pager.
Right-click and Activate it to receive a unique number, then Open it to read and send short text pages anywhere on the map.
Pagers are the long-range tier: use voice chat up close and walkie-talkies at medium range.

An electronics magazine with schematics for a pager relay tower.
Read it to learn how to craft one (needs Electricity 5).

A pager relay tower.
Right-click it to set up the tower at your feet, then power it from a nearby generator.
In tower signal mode the pager network only works while a set-up tower has electricity.
